analysis.brief_en: The proposed Rabies Eradication and Dog Registration Bill in Sri Lanka has raised concerns among the Public Health Inspectors Association (PHIA), which warns that the legislation could disrupt the country’s dog vaccination drive and increase the risk of human rabies. The bill, which is under review by the government, requires dog vaccination to be conducted by veterinarians or under their supervision. However, the current vaccination programme relies on Public Health Inspectors (PHIs) and Medical Officers of Health (MOH) to reach communities, including stray dogs and domestic dogs. PHIA argues that the absence of veterinarians in MOH-level services and the exclusion of PHIs from enforcement could hinder the programme’s effectiveness. The Ministry of Health has noted that dogs are the main reservoir for rabies and responsible for most human rabies deaths, with 20 laboratory-confirmed cases reported in 2024. The association supports rabies eradication but urges amendments to ensure the bill is practical and does not derail existing efforts. The World Health Organization has recognized dog vaccination and post-exposure prophylaxis as critical interventions in reducing human rabies deaths, which have dropped significantly over the years. The bill’s implementation remains uncertain, with calls for review and adjustments before it becomes law.

title: Feds fight rabies amid concerning rise in animal cases, human exposures

analysis.time: The CDC issued a Health Alert Network advisory last week, and as of September 2, 2026, utilization of rabies vaccines and immunoglobulins has increased by 33% and 76%, respectively, compared with the same time period last year. The USDA plans to distribute the vaccine in October, and the Minnesota Board of Animal Health confirmed a cow tested positive for rabies last week.
analysis.location_and_population: The events are reported in the United States, specifically in the Southeast region for the USDA airdrop and in Minnesota for the cow rabies case. The affected population includes wildlife, domestic animals, and humans who have been exposed to rabid animals.
analysis.event: The CDC reported a 17% increase in questions about human exposures to rabid or possibly rabid animals in July and August 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. The USDA is conducting an annual airdrop of rabies vaccines over the Southeast to immunize wildlife. A cow in Brown County, Minnesota, tested positive for rabies, leading to quarantine and PEP recommendations.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The CDC received reports from at least eight state health departments of increased rabies PEP use, administration errors, or both. In Minnesota, less than 15% of rabid animal cases occur in domestic species, with cattle, cats, and dogs being the most common. Over 40 cattle, a vaccinated horse, and three unvaccinated dogs are under observation. The cost of each PEP course is up to $14,000.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The USDA is distributing oral rabies vaccine sachets via airplane, helicopter, and motor vehicle over targeted areas in October. The Minnesota Board of Animal Health confirmed the cow case and urged the use of personal protective equipment when interacting with animals that could have rabies. The CDC is monitoring the situation and has not acknowledged any 2026 rabies deaths yet.

analysis.brief_en: The CDC has raised concerns about a 17% increase in questions about human exposures to rabid or possibly rabid animals in July and August 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. As of September 2, 2026, utilization of rabies vaccines and immunoglobulins has increased by 33% and 76%, respectively, compared to the previous year. The USDA is conducting an annual airdrop of millions of fishmeal-coated rabies vaccine sachets over the Southeast to immunize wildlife against rabies. In Minnesota, a cow tested positive for rabies, leading to the quarantine of 13 cows and PEP recommendations for nine people. The Minnesota Board of Animal Health noted that less than 15% of rabid animal cases occur in domestic species, with cattle, cats, and dogs being the most common. Officials are urging the use of personal protective equipment when handling animals that may have rabies. The USDA plans to move the raccoon vaccine distribution area east as rabies is eliminated locally and regionally. Each PEP course costs up to $14,000.

title: Amid new CDC advisory, AVMA details recent rabies exposure incidents, reiterates vaccination policy

analysis.time: September 14, 2026 (publication date); the CDC advisory was issued on September 10, 2026, and the incidents were reported from July through August 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Multiple US states, including North Carolina, Maryland, New Jersey, and New Hampshire; the affected population includes humans and animals, with specific incidents involving goats, beavers, raccoons, and foxes or fishers.
analysis.event: Several rabies exposure incidents were reported across multiple states, including an outbreak linked to a traveling petting zoo in North Carolina and attacks by rabid animals in Maryland, New Jersey, and New Hampshire. The AVMA reiterated its rabies vaccination policy following a CDC advisory on increased human exposures and PEP administration errors.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: At least 8 state health departments reported increased rabies PEP use, administration errors, or both over the past 3 months. In North Carolina, more than 260 people were advised to receive PEP. As of September 2, 2026, rabies vaccine and human rabies immune globulin use had increased by 33% and 76%, respectively, compared to the same period in 2025. Annually, about 1.4 million people seek medical care after suspected contact with rabid animals, and approximately 100,000 receive PEP. Fewer than 10 human rabies deaths are reported annually in the US.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The CDC issued a health advisory on September 10, 2026, and health departments reported increased PEP use and errors. The AVMA reiterated its vaccination policy and endorsed the 2016 Compendium of Animal Rabies Prevention and Control. The situation is under investigation, with no confirmed cases of rabies in humans or animals reported in the supplied evidence.

From July through August 2026, the CDC received 17% more rabies-related inquiries than in the same period in 2025. As of September 2, 2026, use of rabies vaccines and immune globulin products had increased by 33% and 76%, respectively. The AVMA reiterated its vaccination policy and endorsed the 2016 Compendium of Animal Rabies Prevention and Control. While no confirmed human rabies cases were reported, the incidents underscore the importance of vaccination and PEP in preventing the spread of rabies. The situation remains under investigation, with health departments monitoring increased PEP use and administration errors.
